items.stem: In perspective drawing, the horizon line always represents…
items.explanation: Raise the horizon for a bird's-eye view, lower it for a worm's-eye view.

distractors.d: The ground plane runs towards it.

items.stem: Looking straight down a long, straight road, how many vanishing points are there?
items.explanation: Parallel lines going away from you meet at a single vanishing point on the horizon.

items.stem: In two-point perspective, vertical lines…

options.text: Meet at a third vanishing point

items.explanation: Only horizontal edges recede to the two vanishing points; verticals stay vertical.

items.stem: Where do the vanishing points sit in two-point perspective?

options.text: One above and one below the horizon
At the corners of the page

items.explanation: Horizontal edges of objects on level ground recede to points on the horizon.
items.takeaway: Vanishing points live on the horizon.

items.stem: Drawing a skyscraper from street level looking up usually needs…
items.explanation: Looking up, verticals also converge towards a third vanishing point high above.

distractors.c: That's for facing a flat surface.

items.stem: Two people of the same height stand on flat ground, one near and one far. If the viewer is also standing, where are their heads?

options.text: The far person's head is far below the horizon
The near person's head is far above the page

items.explanation: When eye levels are the same, standing people's eyes and heads line up with the horizon whatever their distance; only their size changes.

distractors.c: Heads stay on the horizon when eye levels match.

items.takeaway: Same height → heads on the horizon.

items.stem: Isometric drawing differs from perspective because…

options.text: It only shows the top view
Parallel lines stay parallel and there are no vanishing points

items.explanation: Isometric uses axes 120° apart; it's great for technical clarity but doesn't show distance like perspective.

items.stem: A circle drawn on the floor in perspective looks like…

options.text: An ellipse whose long axis is horizontal

items.explanation: Circles on horizontal surfaces become horizontal ellipses, flatter as they get closer to eye level.

distractors.c: Perspective doesn't change circles into squares.

items.stem: The ellipse of a glass's rim looks flattest when the rim is…
items.explanation: Ellipses get rounder the further they are from eye level. Draw a cup's top ellipse flatter than its base if the cup is below your eyes.

distractors.c: It looks rounder when you look down on it.

items.takeaway: Closer to eye level = flatter ellipse.

items.stem: An arm pointing straight at the viewer appears…

options.text: Short, with the hand looking large

items.explanation: Foreshortening compresses length towards the viewer and enlarges the nearer parts.

distractors.d: Length shrinks along the line of sight.

items.takeaway: Pointing at you = short and big-ended.

items.stem: The best way to draw a strongly foreshortened limb is to…

options.text: Use overlapping shapes, with the near parts larger
Outline it with one long line

items.explanation: Overlapping ellipses and circles, plus size change, create a convincing foreshortened form.

items.stem: The brightest spot on a shiny object, facing the light, is called the…
items.explanation: Highlights show the light's direction and the surface's shininess.

distractors.b: That's the darkest band on the object.
distractors.c: That's a glow in the shadow side.

items.stem: The darkest band on a sphere, between its lit and shadow sides, is the…
items.explanation: Light → highlight → mid-tone → core shadow → reflected light → cast shadow. Getting this order right makes forms look round.
items.takeaway: Core shadow sits at the turning edge.

items.stem: A low sun (morning or evening) produces shadows that are…
items.explanation: Shadow length depends on the light's height: low light, long shadows.

items.stem: Faint light bouncing into an object's shadow side from nearby surfaces is called…
items.explanation: Reflected light keeps shadows from looking flat. Keep it darker than any lit area.
items.takeaway: Reflected light: subtle, in the shadow.

items.stem: If a cast shadow falls towards the viewer, the light source is…
items.explanation: Shadows point away from the light. Backlighting throws shadows towards you and makes rims glow.

distractors.d: Then the shadow would fall away from you.
distractors.a: Then the shadow would be underneath.

items.takeaway: Shadow points away from the light.

items.stem: An average adult human figure is about how many heads tall?
items.explanation: Using the head as a unit makes proportions easier to check.

items.stem: With arms hanging at the sides, an adult's fingertips usually reach…
items.explanation: Elbows at the waist, wrists at the hips, fingertips at mid-thigh.

items.stem: Compared with adults, young children have…

options.text: Smaller heads relative to their bodies
Longer legs relative to their bodies
Larger heads relative to their bodies

items.explanation: A young child is about 4–6 heads tall. Drawing children with adult proportions makes them look like small adults.

items.stem: The 'line of action' in figure drawing is…

options.text: One curved line showing the main flow of the pose

items.explanation: Starting with a line of action (usually the spine) makes poses dynamic instead of stiff.

items.stem: Stippling is a shading technique that uses…
items.explanation: Denser dots make darker tones. Stippling suits stone, sand and soft textures.

items.stem: Cross-hatching creates darker tones by…
items.explanation: More layers of crossing lines create darker values.

items.stem: To make polished steel look shiny in a pencil drawing, you should…

options.text: Use strong contrast: sharp dark reflections next to bright highlights

items.explanation: Reflective surfaces show sharp, high-contrast reflections of their surroundings.

items.stem: In line drawing, thicker lines are typically used for…

options.text: Edges closer to the viewer or in shadow

items.explanation: Varying line weight adds depth: heavy for near and shadowed edges, light for far and lit edges.

items.stem: Construction lines in a drawing should be…

options.text: Light, so they can be erased or ignored

items.explanation: Light guide lines help get proportions and perspective right without ruining the final drawing.

distractors.a: Dark construction lines are hard to hide.

items.takeaway: Guide lines light; final lines confident.

items.stem: A 'contour drawing' focuses on…

options.text: The edges and outlines of forms

items.explanation: Contour drawing trains observation of edges; blind contour (not looking at the paper) sharpens hand–eye coordination.

items.stem: To make a crowd look deep in a scene, which technique helps MOST?

options.text: Overlap and making far figures smaller

items.explanation: Overlap and diminishing size are the two strongest depth cues in drawing.

items.stem: Without a cast shadow, an object drawn on a table often looks like it is…
items.explanation: A cast shadow, especially the dark contact shadow, connects the object to the surface.

items.stem: In one-point perspective, how many vanishing points are there?

options.text: Two, at the ends of the page

items.explanation: Lines going straight back from the viewer all meet at a single vanishing point on the horizon.

distractors.d: Parallel lines going back meet at one point.

items.stem: When drawing a cube in two-point perspective, the vertical edges should be…
items.explanation: Two-point perspective uses two vanishing points for width and depth; verticals stay vertical.

distractors.d: Then they'd not be vertical edges.

items.stem: The horizon line in a drawing always matches the…
items.explanation: Moving your eye level up or down moves the horizon line. Above it you see the underside of things; below it, the top.

distractors.b: Height of objects doesn't set it.

items.stem: You are drawing a tall building while looking up from the street. Which perspective helps most?

options.text: Three-point perspective, with a vanishing point above

items.explanation: Looking up, the verticals converge too, so a third vanishing point above the building adds drama.

distractors.d: Won't show the building narrowing upward.
distractors.b: Verticals would stay parallel and look flat.

items.stem: Equal-sized lamp posts along a road appear in perspective…

options.text: Smaller and closer together as they go back
The same size all the way
Further apart as they go back

items.explanation: Both size and spacing shrink towards the vanishing point.

items.stem: An arm pointing straight at the viewer looks shorter than its real length. This is called…
items.explanation: When a form points towards you, its length compresses. Overlapping shapes and size change sell the effect.

distractors.b: It's an optical effect, not a choice.
distractors.c: Proportion is size relationships in general.

items.stem: When drawing a foreshortened hand reaching towards the viewer, the fingertips should be drawn…

options.text: Larger than usual, overlapping the palm

items.explanation: The nearest part is drawn largest and overlaps parts behind it.

items.stem: The darkest part of the shadow on an object (not the cast shadow) is called the…
items.explanation: The core shadow sits where the form turns away from the light, just before reflected light.

distractors.d: That's light bouncing back into the shadow.

items.takeaway: Core shadow = darkest band on the form.

items.stem: Why is there a faint lighter area inside the shadow side of a ball on a white table?

options.text: Light bounces off the table back onto the ball (reflected light)

items.explanation: Reflected light is always darker than the lit side, but lifts the shadow and suggests roundness.

distractors.a: It's observed and makes forms look round.
distractors.b: The highlight is on the lit side.

items.stem: The cast shadow of an object is darkest and sharpest…

options.text: Right where the object touches the ground

items.explanation: The contact point (occlusion shadow) is the darkest, anchoring the object to the surface.

distractors.b: Shadows soften and lighten with distance.
distractors.c: Cast shadows fall away from the light.

items.stem: Light comes from the top left. Where does the cast shadow of a cube fall?

options.text: To the bottom right, away from the light

items.explanation: Shadows fall on the side opposite the light source.

distractors.a: Only if the light is directly overhead.

items.takeaway: Shadow points away from the light.

items.stem: Hatching means shading using…
items.explanation: Hatching builds tone with parallel lines; closer lines look darker.

items.stem: Shading made entirely of small dots is called…
items.explanation: Stippling builds tone by dot density.

items.stem: To show the texture of tree bark in pencil, the best approach is…

options.text: Varied, rough marks following the bark's grain, with dark crevices

items.explanation: Texture is shown by marks that copy the surface's pattern, plus strong contrast in the cracks.

distractors.c: That reads as metal or plastic.

items.stem: Which pencil is best for very dark, rich shadows?
items.explanation: B pencils are softer and darker; the higher the number, the darker. H pencils are harder and lighter.

distractors.a: H pencils are hard and light.

items.stem: How would you show the difference between a glass bottle and a clay pot in pencil?

options.text: Glass: sharp, bright highlights and hard edges; clay: soft, gradual tones and a matte surface
Draw both with the same smooth tone

items.explanation: Shiny surfaces show crisp highlights and reflections; matte ones show soft gradual changes.

distractors.c: Glass is often light with crisp darks.

items.stem: In basic figure drawing, an adult's height is often measured as about…
items.explanation: Artists use the head as a unit; adults are roughly 7½ heads tall.

items.stem: A quick gesture drawing should mainly capture…

options.text: The action and flow of the pose

items.explanation: Gesture drawings take 30 seconds to 2 minutes and show movement with a few flowing lines.

distractors.a: Gesture is about the whole body.

items.stem: When a person stands with weight on one leg, the hips and shoulders usually…
items.explanation: This counter-tilt (contrapposto) makes standing poses look natural and balanced.

items.stem: In a crowd scene, how do you make some people look far away?

options.text: Draw them smaller, higher up near the horizon, with less detail
Draw them lower on the page

items.explanation: Size, position relative to the horizon and detail all signal distance.

distractors.d: Further people move up toward the horizon.
distractors.a: Distant forms get lighter and softer.

items.stem: A line that changes from thick to thin is said to have…
items.explanation: Varying line weight adds life and can show depth: thicker lines feel nearer or in shadow.

distractors.b: Perspective is about depth from vanishing points.

items.stem: In a line drawing, thicker outlines on the underside of objects usually suggest…
items.explanation: Heavier lines where objects rest or turn away from light make them feel grounded.

distractors.c: Thicker lines suggest shadow, not light.

items.stem: A contour drawing done without looking at the paper is called a…
items.explanation: Blind contour trains the eye-hand link by forcing slow, careful observation.

distractors.d: Gesture looks at both and focuses on action.

items.stem: Why do designers draw quick thumbnails before the final drawing?

options.text: To explore many compositions and ideas fast before committing
Because examiners ask for tiny drawings only
Because small drawings get more marks

items.explanation: Thumbnails let you compare layouts in seconds; pick the strongest one to develop.

distractors.c: Saving time and choosing well is the point.
distractors.d: Final drawings should be well sized.

items.takeaway: Many small ideas, then one big one.

items.stem: A circle drawn on the floor in perspective appears as…

options.text: An ellipse, flatter the closer it is to eye level

items.explanation: Circles in perspective become ellipses; at eye level they flatten to a line.
